title: 1986 AHSME Problem 22
statement: Six distinct integers are picked at random from \(\{1,2,3,\ldots,10\}.\) What is the probability that, among those selected, the second smallest is \(3?\)

solutions.text:
There are \(\binom{10}{6}=210\) possible sets. If the second-smallest element is \(3,\) then \(3\) is selected, one element is chosen from \(\{1,2\},\) and four are chosen from \(\{4,5,\ldots,10\}.\) This gives \[ 2\binom74=70 \] favorable sets. The probability is \(\frac{70}{210}=\frac{1}{3}.\)

Thus the correct answer is C.
